proposal.name: Run Go acceptance in prepared Docker environments

plan.name: Run Go acceptance in prepared Docker environments
plan.summary: Complete step 3 of parent #564 in one plumbing change: make the Go environment returned by DockerDependencyRunner.OpenChecks implement RepositoryProcessTransport and RunAcceptance, using the existing Select, Discover, Go producer, collector and repository lifecycle for real base failures and candidate passes with unchanged invocation IDs, identities, packages, arguments and digests; compiler failures remain setup refusals. Lazily stage host-owned helpers outside the candidate tree and compile a standard-library Go transport helper using only the prepared image's tools: the helper owns separate workload stdout, stderr and event pipes and sends framed opaque channels and process status over its own Docker connection, with no framework interpretation, candidate-supplied authority, Python, installation, network or host mounts, preserving literal arguments, captured readonly/vendor policy, disposable caches and the existing offline environment. Keep one environment per part, preserve Run/ReadFile/Close and non-Go behavior, and share the existing twelve-minute run and ten-minute phase shortened by caller and preparer, with bounded uncanceled cleanup joining owned processes, removing the container before its staging and retaining the queue slot until cleanup finishes; setup, transport, cancellation and cleanup errors veto qualification without erasing earlier evidence. Add separate daemon-free runtime fixtures that replace only the Docker boundary, run real Go and the production transport helper, inspect actual Docker arguments and exercise the shared lifecycle and queue, while leaving all existing tests and fakes unchanged and keeping the earlier real-Go tests mandatory; also add a documented offline opt-in against an already prepared pinned Go image that checks base failure, correction, exact children, skip, abrupt exit and forged output, reports missing prerequisites without downloading, and never enables default adapters, configured planning or external plumbing. Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and the README's linked overview to describe the completed Docker runtime capability and remaining compiler-attribution limit, cite the recorded grounds including D-0311, D-0314, D-0316, D-0321, D-0327 and D-0334, keep the README within 400 lines and legacy Go unchanged, and leave recording the Docker transport refinement and unavailable Docker/network verification to the merger while affected real Python and TLAPS suites remain CI requirements.

tests.name: TestDockerGoPreparedRuntime591
tests.says: A prepared Docker Go environment supplies the common process transport and RunAcceptance; real base assertions and production-only corrections yield exact bound evidence while literal selectors, private helpers, offline Docker arguments and existing non-Go behavior are preserved.

tests.name: TestDockerGoRepositoryOutcomes591
tests.says: The configured base and candidate paths use the real Go producer through Docker for independent exact test outcomes, including skip, abrupt exit, forged output and compiler setup refusal, without enabling planning or default adapters.

tests.name: TestDockerGoTransportVetoes591
tests.says: Docker startup, broken or truncated transport and cleanup failures veto qualification, retain earlier authentic evidence and diagnostics, and remove private resources.

tests.name: TestDockerGoLifetimeAndQueue591
tests.says: Parts run one at a time under inherited run, phase and preparer deadlines; cancellation retains running evidence, and the shared queue keeps its slot through uncanceled process, container and staging cleanup, including cleanup failures.

tests.name: TestDockerGoOfflineReal591
tests.says: The default Docker-boundary control must pass, and an explicit opt-in runs the same production transport offline in an existing prepared pinned image for base failure, fix, exact child, skip, abrupt exit and forged-output cases, refusing unavailable prerequisites without downloading.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and acceptance tests, adding only the requested checked `queue.Close()` before the final `b.clean()` and preserving everything else. Check 1 passed: the plan is valid, and all five acceptance tests fail on the unchanged base as required.
